conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Hey, I'm 67 years old and male. I injured my right shoulder a few days ago while playing tackle football with some friends. It's been bothering me ever since, and I wanted to get it checked out.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the mechanism of injury in more detail, such as how the injury occurred and whether there was any direct impact or fall?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Sure, so I was playing tackle football, and I got tackled a couple of times. One time, I landed on my shoulder kind of weird, and that's when it started hurting. I tried to keep playing, but it's been bothering me ever since.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, weakness, or limited range of motion in your right shoulder or arm since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yeah, I haven't had any numbness or tingling in my fingers, but my shoulder does hurt when I try to lift it up to my ear. It's been hard to lift anything heavy, like a box from the driveway, and it's been pretty consistent pain since it happened.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weakness in your right arm or difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing or reaching behind your back?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't had any real trouble with daily activities like dressing, but reaching down to pick up something heavy has been tough. I can still grab a cup of coffee, but I'm trying to avoid lifting anything too heavy.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any swelling, bruising, or deformity in the right shoulder area since the injury occurred?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't recall any swelling or bruising, but there's definitely some pain when I touch the back of my shoulder, near the collarbone area. It doesn't look deformed, but it's been sore and tender since the injury.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the exact location of the tenderness on your shoulder and whether you have experienced any popping or clicking sensations during movement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The tenderness is on the back side of my shoulder, right around the collarbone area. I haven't noticed any popping or clicking when I move it, just pain when I touch it or try to lift my arm up.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arm or hand since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any numbness or tingling in my arm or hand since the injury. My arm still feels strong enough to grab a cup of coffee, but I'm avoiding lifting anything too heavy because it hurts.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any weakness in your right arm or difficulty performing tasks that require fine motor skills, such as buttoning a shirt or writing?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any weakness in my right arm or trouble with fine motor skills like buttoning a shirt or writing. I can still manage those things, but lifting anything heavy is tough and causes pain.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior imaging studies or evaluations of your shoulder, such as X-rays or an MRI, following this injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any prior imaging studies or evaluations of my shoulder following this injury. This is the first time I've been checked out for it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays, MRI, or CT scans for your right shoulder injury? If not, would you be willing to undergo imaging to better evaluate the extent of the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any imaging studies for my right shoulder injury yet. But I'm willing to undergo imaging, like the CAT scan you mentioned, to get a better look at what's going on.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide the results of any prior imaging studies of the shoulder, if available? If not, would you be willing to undergo an X-ray or MRI to evaluate for possible fractures, dislocations, or soft tissue injuries?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I haven't had any imaging studies for my shoulder yet, but I'm willing to get the CAT scan you mentioned to check it out and see what's going on.

conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe the specific limitations you're experiencing with your right shoulder's range of motion, such as how far you can lift your arm or rotate it?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
